This commit addresses an issue where using NA in conjunction with the mask() method that resulted in unexpected behavior. The problem arose when comparing a Series containing NA as a condition within mask(), causing inconsistencies in the output. This fix ensures that NA behaves consistently as False in logical operations within mask().

issue_context.title: ENH: Processing of .mask() for pd.NA
issue_context.body:
### Feature Type

- [ ] Adding new functionality to pandas

- [X] Changing existing functionality in pandas

- [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas


### Problem Description

```python
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        'A': [0, 1, 2]
    },
)
```
For example, suppose you have a DataFrame like the one above.

```python
>>> df[
...     pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]) < 0
... ]
	A
0	0
```
This works as expected.

```python
>>>df[
...     pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]).convert_dtypes() < 0
... ]
	A
0	0
```
This also works as expected.

```python
>>> df['A'].mask(
...     pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]) < 0,
...     100
... )

0    100
1      1
2      2
Name: A, dtype: int64
```
This also works as expected.

```python
>>> df['A'].mask(
...     pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]).convert_dtypes() < 0,
...     100
... )

0    100
1      1
2    100  # !?
Name: A, dtype: int64
```
This behavior confuses a lot of people.


### Feature Description

I think most people would expect this result.
```python
>>> df['A'].mask(
...     pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]).convert_dtypes() < 0,
...     100
... )
0    100
1      1
2      2
Name: A, dtype: int64
```


I think you should either set the result of the logical operation on pd.NA to False 
```python
>>> pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]).convert_dtypes() < 0
0     True
1    False
2    False
dtype: boolean
```
or change the .mask() method to make pd.NA behave the same as False.



### Alternative Solutions

Using .fillna(False) will do what you expect, but I think it would be a depressing task for many people.
```python
>>> df['A'].mask(
...     (pd.Series([-1, 1, pd.NA]).convert_dtypes() < 0).fillna(False),
...     100
... )
0    100
1      1
2      2
Name: A, dtype: int64
```

### Additional Context

_No response_
comments: Thanks for the bug report. Yea seems like mask is not properly handing pd.NA from your OP - pull requests to fix are always welcome!

review_comments: To pass the tests, I think `dtype=BooleanDtype()` should be used here, and from pandas import `BooleanDtype` at the top of the file, just like other dtypes.

Rather than a fillna like this do you see where the logic is breaking down that causes `.mask` to treat `pd.NA` the same was as `True`? We shouldn't have to mess around with pd.NA equality semantics for this fix

For indexing this goes through `check_array_indexer` which essentially also converts NA to False (but lower in the stack):

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/2aa155ae1cf019e902441463d1af873eaa3c803b/pandas/core/indexers/utils.py#L532-L534
